examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: Polite or plural 'you'. Spoken French det expression meaning 'your', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Laissez vos photos et votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les

Informal for cela. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'that'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

En été = in summer. Masculine noun ('le été', plural 'les étés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'summer'.

examples.text: Été deux mille onze. Elle s'est cassé la cheville.
examples.trans: Summer twenty eleven. She broke her ankle.

meanings.note: The most common verb. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
Ce + est. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.

examples.text: Mes amies en parlent tout le temps.
examples.trans: My friends talk about it all the time.
